title: Relational vs NoSQL databases

kcs.statement: A relational database stores data in tables with a fixed schema, links rows by keys and is queried with SQL, supporting joins and multi-row transactions.
NoSQL databases (key-value, document, graph, in-memory) use flexible schemas and scale horizontally, giving up complex joins in exchange for speed at very large scale.

problem_ideas: An order system needs joins across customers, orders and products in one transaction: which family?
A shopping-cart service stores one JSON blob per user and serves millions of users: which family?
Sort cue phrases ('SQL', 'flexible schema', 'joins', 'key-value', 'single-digit ms at any scale') into two columns
A product catalogue where each item has different attributes: why does a fixed schema hurt?

True or false: NoSQL means the database cannot be queried at all
